item.title: Microsoft Begins Automatic Windows 11 26H2 Upgrade Rollout
item.description:
Microsoft Begins Automatic Windows 11 26H2 Upgrade Rollout

Starting this week, Microsoft has begun automatically upgrading eligible devices that aren’t managed by an IT department to Windows 11 26H2.

🔍 Overview

  • Windows 11 26H2 is also known as the Windows 11 2026 Update.
  • It contains all the recently announced features in Windows 11, versions 25H2 and 24H2.

⚙️ Key details

  • It is delivered using servicing technology, providing a fast installation experience.
  • Windows 11 26H2 became generally available in September 2026 as an enablement package.
  • It is scheduled to reach end of support in October 2029.

🚀 Availability

  • Automatic upgrade is available for personal and non-managed business devices running Windows 11 24H2 and 25H2.
  • Automatic delivery is being gradually expanded, starting with devices running Windows 11, versions 24H2 and 25H2, that are not managed by IT departments.
  • Manual installation can be performed via Settings > Windows Update by checking for Windows updates.

💡 Why it matters

  • As the rollout progresses, more Windows 11 devices will upgrade automatically without users having to check for updates manually.
  • Since late October 2026, all devices eligible to run Windows 11 have been able to get version 26H2 by manually checking for updates.

item.title: New Framework for Edge AI Hardware and Model Selection
item.description:
New Framework for Edge AI Hardware and Model Selection

The rapid growth of deep learning has driven the deployment of computer vision directly on resource-constrained edge devices. However, the extreme heterogeneity of edge hardware architectures poses major challenges in selecting and designing suitable vision models. This survey bridges the gap between edge hardware constraints, model architectures, and deployment software toolchains.

🔍 Overview

The study addresses the difficulty of deploying computer vision models across diverse edge environments. By analyzing the relationship between hardware capabilities and model requirements, the research provides a structured approach to overcoming the fragmentation of edge computing resources.

🧩 Hardware Taxonomy

The research establishes a comprehensive taxonomy classifying edge hardware into three distinct tiers:

Hardware Tier Description
Mid-range devices GPUs and dedicated NPUs or TPUs
Dedicated embedded MPU or SoC processors
Microcontrollers MCUs

📊 Benchmark Scope

The analysis aggregates and analyzes multi-source benchmark results for specific tasks:

  • Tasks: Image classification and object detection
  • Power Range: Spanning from tens of watts down to milliwatt-scale bare-metal MCUs

🛠️ Proposed Framework

Based on empirical findings, the study proposes a two-tiered hardware-to-model mapping framework. This framework provides:

  • Model Selection Matrices: Concrete guidance across performance priorities (Speed, Balanced, Accuracy)
  • Architectural Design Principles: Actionable guidelines including peak SRAM budgeting, resolution-first scaling, and algorithm-compiler co-design

⚠️ Challenges & Future

The authors highlight critical deployment challenges and outline future directions:

  • Current Challenges: Toolchain fragmentation, operator incompatibility, and Vision Transformer feasibility
  • Future Research: On-device adaptation and sustainable Edge AI

item.title: OpenClaw Updates Memory Plugin with LanceDB for Persistent AI Context
item.description:
OpenClaw Updates Memory Plugin with LanceDB for Persistent AI Context

OpenClaw has released an update to its memory plugin, now enhanced with LanceDB for persistent, cross-session memory capabilities.

🔍 Overview

The plugin provides a brain that remembers across sessions, agents, and time. It stores preferences, decisions, and project context.

🧩 How it works

  • Classification: LLM-powered 6-category classification (profiles, preferences, entities, events, cases, patterns).
  • Retention: Weibull decay model ensures important memories stay while noise fades.
  • Retrieval: Hybrid Retrieval (Vector + BM25) fused with Cross-Encoder Reranking.
  • Automation: Relevant memories automatically surface before each reply.

⚙️ Key details

  • Version: v1.1.0-beta.10.
  • Architecture: Fully adapted for OpenClaw 2026.3+ new plugin architecture.
  • Hooks: Uses before_prompt_build hooks (replacing deprecated before_agent_start).
  • Isolation: Per-agent, per-user, and per-project memory boundaries.
  • CPU Requirement: CPU must support AVX instructions.
  • Compatibility: LanceDB native vector search may require AVX2 on some Linux x64 builds and can crash AVX-only CPUs with SIGILL.

🚀 Availability

  • Installation: Run npm i memory-lancedb-pro@beta.
  • Setup: Use the community-maintained setup script.
  • Configuration: Add the plugin’s install directory as an absolute path in plugins.load.paths in openclaw.json.
  • Post-Upgrade: Run openclaw doctor --fix after upgrading.
  • API: Supports OpenAI, Jina, Gemini, Ollama, or any OpenAI-compatible API.
  • Fallback: Set retrieval.disableNativeCosine: true or MEMORY_LANCEDB_DISABLE_NATIVE_COSINE=1 to use a scoped row scan plus JavaScript cosine ranking.

item.title: Agent2API: AI Routing Gateway with Unified Model API and Client Takeover
item.description:
Agent2API: AI Routing Gateway with Unified Model API and Client Takeover

Agent2API is an AI routing gateway with Agent client takeover capabilities. It exposes a unified model API for custom AI providers and centralizes account routing, model mapping, gateway keys, and request reports. The platform also manages local Agent clients’ connection profiles, including importing, switching, and previewing configuration changes.

🔍 Overview

Agent2API offers a unified model API for OpenAI (Chat, Responses, Images) and Anthropic (Messages), alongside a unified model catalog. It functions as an AI assistant tool that manages multiple connection profiles for local clients, allowing users to import existing settings, preview writes, and switch between the gateway and custom services.

⚙️ Key Features

  • AI Routing: The system handles model mapping, account priority, load balancing, session affinity, and failover in one place.
  • Plugin Extensions: Additional provider implementations are installed and updated separately and are not bundled with the application. Custom providers do not require them.
  • Egress Proxies: Users can select proxy-pool exits for accounts and update tasks.
  • Gateway Security: Features include scoped gateway keys, optional human verification for panel sign-in, and model requests refused by default until a key is configured.
  • Request Reports: The dashboard provides metrics on request volume, success rate, token usage, cache hit rate, and a 365-day heatmap.
  • Background Maintenance: The system performs model catalog refreshes, credential maintenance, and software update checks. Daily check-ins run per provider on specific windows (e.g., Qoder at 10:01, ZCode at 19:01), with a catch-up round for unchecked accounts.

🚀 Availability

  • Deployment Forms: Available as Windows, macOS, and Linux desktop apps, as well as headless Windows and Linux servers, and Docker containers (amd64 and arm64). It requires no Node runtime and supports a six-language interface.
  • ProxyLane Integration: ProxyLane provides native static residential ISP proxies for AI accounts. These IPs come from real home broadband operators with low Scamalytics fraud scores. Each IP is dedicated to the user with unlimited traffic, starting at $3.90.

🌐 Community and Support

  • Access: Users can join QQ groups (Agent2API chat groups) or the Telegram group.
  • Contact: Email is available at 541675139@qq.com.
  • Promotion: A 25% discount is available using the code AGENT2API25.

item.title: Community Agent Skill Restores Codex Desktop Capabilities on Windows
item.description:
Community Agent Skill Restores Codex Desktop Capabilities on Windows

A new community-maintained Agent Skill has been released to guide AI assistants in restoring local patches and capability switches for Codex Desktop on Windows following updates. This tool provides diagnostic workflows and repair scripts to fix issues such as missing model lists, browser functionality, and computer control features.

🔍 Overview

  • Purpose: Guides agents to restore local patches and capability switches after updates.
  • Scope: Fixes model lists, browser, and computer control (computer use) features.
  • Nature: Community-maintained Agent Skill (diagnosis + scripts), not an official client or universal installer.
  • Platform: Windows only.

🛠️ Installation

  • Prerequisites: Windows Codex Desktop, Git, and an AI assistant that supports Agent Skills.
  • Setup Command: 
    1
2

    $SkillRoot = "$env:USERPROFILE\.codex\skills\codex-windows-fast-patch"
git clone https://github.com/chen0416ccc-cpu/codex-windows-fast-patch-skill.git $SkillRoot
  • Paths:
    • Standard: $env:USERPROFILE\.codex\skills\codex-windows-fast-patch
    • Claude Code: $env:USERPROFILE\.claude\skills\codex-windows-fast-patch
  • Activation: Restart the AI assistant to load the skill. The skill updates automatically before use.

🧩 Capabilities & Fixes

  • Proxy Restoration: Restores CUA browser proxy settings. It inherits valid HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY or generates a managed local runtime patch from Windows system proxies.
  • Mobile Control: Optional process. If only the settings entry is missing, a dry-run script can check the route without fixing auth.
  • General Repairs: Fixes model lists, browser, and computer control. Some fixes require reinstalling Codex.
  • Limitations:
    • Does not support PAC, authenticated, or non-HTTP proxies.
    • Models are provided by the vendor; the project does not provide API or quotas.
    • Cannot recover deleted project files.

⚙️ Safety & Execution

  • Process: The application may close during repairs, interrupting the conversation. Restart Codex and send “继续” to resume.
  • Verification: Requires a restart and separate verification of Chrome and the built-in browser.
  • Execution Mode: Default is background read-only verification.
  • Safety: Does not automatically open test apps (like calculator), switch focus, or send mouse/keyboard input.
  • Reporting: Runtime, plugin, and window enumeration checks are reported. Real screenshots and native input are only performed upon explicit request or agreement.

item.title: Open WebUI: Self-Hosted Platform for Local AI Models
item.description:
Open WebUI: Self-Hosted Platform for Local AI Models

Open WebUI is a home for AI: an extensible, easy-to-use, self-hosted platform built to run entirely offline. It connects local models through Ollama or uses OpenAI-compatible APIs for local and cloud models.

🔍 Overview

Supported languages include English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Korean, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Danish, Japanese, Polish, Russian, Bosnian, Arabic, Norwegian, Portuguese (Brazil), Thai, Turkish, Ukrainian, Bengali, Greek, and Vietnamese. A native desktop app is available for macOS, Windows, and Linux.

🚀 Installation

Python Installation Run DATA_DIR=~/.open-webui uvx --python 3.12 open-webui@latest serve. The web interface is available at http://localhost:8080.

Pip Installation Run pip install open-webui followed by open-webui serve.

Docker Installation Run docker run -d -p 3000:8080 --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway -v open-webui:/app/backend/data --name open-webui --restart always ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main. The web interface is available at http://localhost:3000.

🐳 Docker Image Variants

Image Tag Description
:main Standard image with local AI dependencies
:slim Lightweight image using external services for embeddings, document extraction, and voice
:cuda Open WebUI with CUDA acceleration
:ollama Open WebUI bundled with Ollama
:dev Latest development build

⚙️ Configuration & Features

Environment Variables

  • OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://your-ollama-server:11434 connects to Ollama on another server.
  • OPENAI_API_KEY=your_secret_key sets the OpenAI API key.
  • HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 disables Hugging Face model downloads for offline use.

GPU Support Use the --gpus all option for Nvidia GPU access with the :cuda or :ollama images. This requires the Nvidia Container Toolkit.

GitHub Information The repository displays stars, forks, watchers, repo size, language count, top language, and last commit date. Social badges link to Discord and GitHub sponsors.

📚 Documentation & Support

  • Documentation: https://docs.openwebui.com/
  • Roadmap: https://docs.openwebui.com/roadmap/
  • Installation Docs: https://docs.openwebui.com/getting-started/
  • Troubleshooting: https://docs.openwebui.com/troubleshooting/
  • Updating Guide: https://docs.openwebui.com/getting-started/updating
  • Support: Available via GitHub issues or discussions.

item.title: DXC OASIS AI Platform Launches with Amazon Bedrock and Guardrails
item.description:
DXC OASIS AI Platform Launches with Amazon Bedrock and Guardrails

DXC Technology launched DXC OASIS, a governed AI agent platform built on Amazon Bedrock, to support mission-critical systems for regulated organizations.

🔍 Overview

DXC OASIS separates the question of which model from the question of how work gets done. The system consists of two layers:

  • Governed model substrate: Built on Amazon Bedrock.
  • Trusted harness: DXC’s own orchestration, governance, and assurance layer.

🧩 How it works

DXC OASIS runs on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) in a private subnet. Engineers and operators access the system via Amazon Route 53 and an Application Load Balancer inside the customer’s Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC).

A supervisor agent delegates tasks to capability agents that draw on a knowledge base, AWS Secrets Manager, Amazon EventBridge, and Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3). Every model call leaves the subnet through a VPC interface endpoint and AWS PrivateLink to reach Amazon Bedrock.

⚙️ Key details

  • Model Access: Through a single managed interface, DXC OASIS accesses multiple foundation models: Anthropic Claude, Amazon Nova, Meta Llama, and open-weight families.
  • Security and Guardrails: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails enforce content filtering, personally identifiable information (PII) redaction, and denied-topic policies uniformly across every model.
  • Data Privacy: Across every model, customer data stays within the AWS data boundary. Prompts and completions are not shared with third-party model providers and are not used to train the underlying foundation models.
  • Observability: AWS Identity and Access Management (AWS IAM), AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS), TLS 1.2, Amazon CloudWatch, VPC Flow Logs, AWS CloudTrail, and OpenTelemetry provide security and observability across every layer.

🚀 Availability

DXC began building DXC OASIS as a prototype in early 2025. A cross-functional team reached general availability in March 2026. Since that time, DXC OASIS has reduced resolution time by 95% on average across 56 measured use cases. The system is scaling toward 130 customer environments on Amazon EKS with per-tenant namespaces and GitOps rollout.

item.title: Amazon Bedrock Adds Web Search API for AI Agents
item.description:
Amazon Bedrock Adds Web Search API for AI Agents

AI agents increasingly handle work that depends on what changed today, such as security advisories, product releases, prices, and regulations. A model’s training data can’t answer those questions, so agents need web search. For production use, teams also need results they can cite, and control over which sources count.

🌐 Overview

The Web Search API in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is now available. It gives agents and applications current web results through a single API call, signed with the AWS credentials they already use.

⚙️ Key Details

  • AWS serves every query from a web index that Amazon operates, and doesn’t send it to a third‑party search engine.
  • Each result includes the page’s title, URL, publication date, and an extract relevant to the query.
  • Requests can include or exclude domains, and limit results to a publication date range.
  • There’s no search API key to store or rotate.
  • Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is also available through AgentCore Gateway.
  • For LangChain developers, the AgentCore web search tool in LangChain’s AWS integration now calls the Web Search API.
  • The tool can also hold rules that the model can’t change, such as a date window, a source blocklist, and a search budget.
  • It works with LangChain agents, with LangGraph, the orchestration framework that runs them, and with Deep Agents, which adds subagents, a virtual filesystem, and context compression.
  • The Web Search API needs one IAM action on one resource that AWS owns, so the statement is the same in every account.
  • Web Search and model calls are billed per use.
  • One run of the watch makes at most 12 searches.

🧩 Use Case: The Watch

Every morning, the watch checks whether anything new affects the open source packages and container base images the team ships. It researches three package ecosystems in parallel, while your code keeps the date window, the blocklist, and the search budget out of the model’s control.

In our test, the three branches finished in 36 seconds, against 99 seconds one after another. A run starts the graph with the watchlist and the watch window. Inside each branch, the agent calls an Anthropic Claude model in Amazon Bedrock. The model decides what to search for and, at the end, produces structured findings.

The branch’s search tool adds the date window and the blocklist to each query. It calls the Web Search API with a request signed with AWS Signature Version 4 (SigV4). Each branch keeps only findings that its sources support and that fall inside the window. The examples use the US East (N. Virginia) Region (us-east-1).

The watch can’t let the model choose the date window, the trusted sources, or the number of searches. Every search carries the blocklist and the date floor, and a model’s own arguments could only narrow them.

🚀 Availability

On AWS Lambda, Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS), or Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime, your agent calls the API with its execution role. One function call gives an agent current, cited search results.

item.title: TCS Launches Agentic Test Orchestrator on AWS for BFSI
item.description:
TCS Launches Agentic Test Orchestrator on AWS for BFSI

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) has introduced the Agentic Test Orchestrator, a multi-tenant SaaS solution designed to automate testing for Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance (BFSI) clients. The platform addresses the bottleneck where slowest part of a release is rarely writing application code, but rather the testing process itself.

🔍 Overview

The Agentic Test Orchestrator decomposes testing into specialized tasks, where each task has its own agent, tools, validation rules, and context. A deterministic supervisor routes work, while an execution workflow controls retries, error classification, persistence, and reporting.

🧩 How it works

The platform accepts inputs from various sources to generate executable tests:

  • Inputs: Jira stories, business requirement documents (BRDs), Swagger specifications, uploaded documents, GitLab source folders, or captured UI flows.
  • Generation: From these inputs, the platform generates test scenarios, Gherkin feature files, and executable Java or Python tests.
  • Execution: It runs those tests on Amazon ECS, stores artifacts and results, and shows progress and reports in a per-tenant web application.

⚙️ Key Details

AWS Services Used

Service Function
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Hosts the platform’s specialized agents built with the Strands Agents SDK. It offers model choice, runtime scaling, and microVM isolation.
Amazon EKS Runs the tenant web application.
Amazon ECS Runs the generated tests.
Amazon S3 & Amazon DynamoDB Store the results.
Amazon CloudWatch Captures the logs.
Security Services AWS WAF, Amazon Cognito, AWS KMS, and AWS Secrets Manager enforce per-tenant security and isolation.

Architecture

The solution is built on a shared control plane and tenant application planes:

  • Shared Control Plane: Provides the Amazon EKS cluster, container registry, administrative portal, tenant registry, onboarding automation, Amazon CloudFront distributions, and AWS WAF protection.
  • Tenant Application Plane: Each tenant receives its own Kubernetes namespace, Amazon Cognito user pool, AWS KMS key, Amazon S3 bucket, Amazon DynamoDB tables, and Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases.

Onboarding Process

The administrative API writes a pending tenant record, emits an event through Amazon EventBridge, and starts an AWS CodeBuild project that deploys the tenant infrastructure with AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK).

💡 Why it matters

For BFSI clients, the platform is designed to meet strict requirements:

  • Context: Every test must be grounded in project-specific context rather than generic prompts.
  • Coverage: It covers both API and browser-based UI testing to match how BFSI applications are built.
  • Security: Every tenant’s data and knowledge store must be isolated.
  • Repeatability: It provides a repeatable path from requirement ingestion to test evidence and reporting.

item.title: LLM Performance and Naming Conventions Explained
item.description:
LLM Performance and Naming Conventions Explained

On October 28, 2026, Ted Sanders provided insights into the complexities of LLM performance and OpenAI’s model naming conventions.

🔍 Overview

In general, LLM performance is incredibly multidimensional. There’s no guarantee of a fixed ordering where the model that is best at math is also the model that’s best at jokes. Despite that complexity, much of the variation in performance is explained by just a single variable: model size.

⚙️ Key Details

In general, models that are bigger will:

  • (a) be more performant / reliable
  • (b) cost more per token
  • (c) have better recall of esoteric facts

As you note, our models are ordered:

Luna < Terra < Sol < Astra

These days, version number signifies a few things at once: the order of release, the relationship to other releases, and the magnitude of improvement. So something like 6.1 would indicate it was launched after 5.6, may share some similarities to other 6.1 models in terms of training data / personality (which is why it’s not 5.7), and isn’t a giant enough leap to merit the headlines and expectations that would come with a 7.

— Ted Sanders, explaining OpenAI’s model naming conventions

Model Order
Luna 1st
Terra 2nd
Sol 3rd
Astra 4th

item.title: Meta Updates Terms to Allow AI Training on Associated Websites
item.description:
Meta Updates Terms to Allow AI Training on Associated Websites

Meta has updated its terms of service to grant itself permission to crawl and scrape websites associated with business accounts for AI training. The new terms, which go into effect on October 30, allow Meta to use outside content to “develop, improve, research,” and “train” its AI products.

🔍 Overview

The policy applies to business accounts that promote their content across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Messenger. It allows Meta to crawl all websites ‘associated’ with a business account. This includes domains, web pages, or URLs that are made available through the business’s use of Meta’s products and services.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Authorization: The terms authorize Meta to use automated software (such as web scrapers, bots, crawlers, and user agents) to access, index, cache, analyze, collect, retrieve, or crawl domains associated with products or services.
  • Usage: Meta may use any content from such domains to provide, develop, improve, research, train, and maintain the integrity of its Meta Company Products and services.
  • Enforcement: Businesses that do not agree to Meta’s new policies “may stop all access or use of our Products for business or commercial purposes.”

🧩 Legal and Industry Context

  • Robots.txt: Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts states there is “no change to how Meta uses web crawlers” and claims content owners can still use robots.txt flags to indicate their preferences.
  • Expert Analysis: Legal experts tell Nieman Lab that this could allow Meta to argue its commercial terms supersede other blocking instructions, like a site’s robots.txt file. This could potentially allow Meta to bypass a licensing agreement and freely train its AI models on content posted by online publishers.
  • Existing Deals: Meta has followed OpenAI in striking AI licensing deals with CNN, Fox News, USA Today, and People Inc., but these new terms could give the company access to a much broader swath of content.
  • Professor Quote: James Grimmelmann, a professor of digital and information law at Cornell, tells Nieman Lab that for news publishers, this clearly represents permission to Meta to train AI on any content from their sites and possibly to deploy some of that content, even in competition with the publishers themselves.

💡 Why It Matters

  • News Sites: The new policy may allow Meta to train AI on news sites for free.
  • Meta’s Stance: Andy Stone, Meta’s vice president of communications, writes in a post on X that this change isn’t meant to target news sites, stating the update is designed to pull accurate information about products for sale on third‑party websites when making on‑platform ad and content recommendations.
  • Cost Implications: Last month, Meta launched a new Meta One subscription that requires businesses and creators to pay to include links in posts and reels. Nieman Lab notes that “Meta has begun charging users to post links to the same content that it will be permitted to crawl for free.”

item.title: Wonderful Thailand CEO Discusses Scaling AI Agents at Techsauce 2026
item.description:
Wonderful Thailand CEO Discusses Scaling AI Agents at Techsauce 2026

Ariya Banomyong, President of Wonderful Thailand, addressed the challenge of moving AI from pilots to production at the Techsauce Global Summit 2026.

📈 Scaling from Pilots to Production

Most organizations are already running AI pilots, but few reach production. Banomyong stated that the constraint is rarely the technology itself, but how organizations are set up to design, deploy, and measure it. He noted that in previous technology cycles—internet adoption, e-commerce, and online video—the technology arrived as expected, and what differed was when organizations chose to act.

🧩 Architecture and Design Strategy

To scale effectively, organizations should avoid building separate agents within each function. Banomyong argued that the value of AI tends to appear across functions rather than within any one of them. When each department funds its own initiative and selects its own provider, the result can be several implementations that were never designed to work together. Solutions built for a sandbox are rarely ready for enterprise volumes or the wider set of use cases a business will want to run on the same foundation. Designing for production scale and multiple use cases from the outset, then piloting within that architecture, reduces later rebuilds.

📊 Use Case Examples

Banomyong illustrated successful deployments with two client examples:

Scenario Agents Involved Key Mechanism Outcome
SME Lending Relationship assistant, lending agent, credit reviewer Context sharing across agents; legacy system integration Chat message moves to booking in core system
Home Broadband Single assistant Camera reads router status lights Customer handled from start to finish without queue jumping

🛡️ Risk and Governance

On risk, Banomyong reframed the discussion around designing safeguards. In Wonderful’s architecture, an observer agent runs in the background to check that other agents operate within policy, governance, and regulatory requirements. Bank Hapoalim in Israel went live within three weeks at 88% containment, meaning roughly 880 of every 1,000 calls or chats were resolved without human involvement. Case studies on Wonderful’s website cite comparable results at 80% or above.

🚀 Company Updates

Wonderful operates in more than 35 markets and recently opened in Thailand with a local team. Founded in 2025 and headquartered in Amsterdam, the company positions its product as an enterprise AI operating system. In September 2026, the company announced a $550 million Series C led by Insight Partners at a $5 billion valuation. The company was also named Official Enterprise AI Partner of FC Bayern in the same month.

⏱️ Delivery Timeline

Deployments generally take four to eight weeks, depending on workflow and integration complexity. Governance, guardrails, and evaluation tooling are in place from the start. Wonderful’s teams work directly with clients to redesign cross-functional workflows, then transfer capability to internal teams who build and manage agents on the same platform.

item.title: Claude Agent SDK vs LangGraph: Control Flow Philosophies
item.description:
Claude Agent SDK vs LangGraph: Control Flow Philosophies

The debate between the Claude Agent SDK and LangGraph is often framed as a product comparison, but it is actually a comparison of two philosophies regarding who should be responsible for an agent’s control flow.

🔍 Overview

The Claude Agent SDK and LangGraph offer different approaches to building AI agents. One hands you a loop, while the other hands you a box of primitives to draw a graph.

🧩 The Claude Agent SDK (The Loop Philosophy)

The Claude Agent SDK hands you a loop. It already knows how to plan, call a tool, read the result, and decide what to do next because it is the same loop that runs Claude Code.

  • How it works: You import it, define your tools, point it at a task, and the loop does the rest: plans, calls tools, reads results, and keeps going until it is finished or you stop it.
  • Capabilities: You get code execution, file manipulation, bash, web browsing, and MCP tool integrations out of the box.
  • Constraints: You do not get a say in how the loop behaves. The retry semantics, the way it decides what to do next, and the order it approaches a problem are all decided. Additionally, every task runs on a Claude model, making it Claude-only.

🧩 LangGraph (The Graph Philosophy)

LangGraph hands you a box of primitives and expects you to draw the graph yourself. You declare nodes, edges, and a shared state schema, and the framework executes the graph until a node returns END.

  • Features: You can write specific logic, such as a node that fans out to five parallel branches, joins them, checks a condition, and loops back twice.
  • Execution: Checkpointers provide durable execution by saving state to persistent storage after every logical step, so a crash or a restart resumes from the last checkpoint. Interrupts allow for real human-in-the-loop capabilities by pausing the graph at a specific node.
  • Tech Stack: It is model-agnostic, supports Python and JavaScript, and plugs into LangSmith for tracing and LangGraph Platform for deployment.
  • Maturity: It is the most widely adopted thing in this space by a wide margin, and that maturity is worth something on its own.

⚙️ Performance and Availability

The Claude Agent SDK is built for speed with ~10ms latency, even under load. It handles 350+ RPS on just 1 vCPU without needing tuning. It is production-ready with full enterprise support.

💡 Which Approach Fits?

Both approaches are defensible. The choice depends on a question most teams answer too late: does your agent actually need a custom topology, or does it just need to work?
